analysis.one_liner: Hindustan Aeronautics (HAL) is the state-owned monopoly designer, manufacturer and maintainer of fighter jets (Tejas, Sukhoi), helicopters (LCH, ALH) and aero-engines for India's armed forces.
analysis.whats_happening: Q1 FY27 (June quarter) results, reported mid-August 2026, showed consolidated revenue of ₹5,515 crore (+14.45% YoY) and PAT of ₹1,589.66 crore (+14.8% YoY), with EBITDA margin expanding to roughly 27.7-28% from 21.6% a year earlier. GE Aerospace has repeatedly missed F404-IN20 engine delivery deadlines (only 3 delivered in August 2026 against a 5-engine commitment), on which HAL has imposed liquidated damages, and this continues to delay Tejas Mk1A handovers to the Air Force. The next results (Q2 FY27) are due at a board meeting on November 3, 2026 - not verified beyond the NSE intimation filed October 7, 2026.
analysis.plain_terms: HAL sits at the centre of India's push to build fighter jets, helicopters and engines at home, and it has a near seven-to-eight-year order pipeline sitting on its books. That is the attractive part. The tension is that the company has struggled for years to turn that order book into delivered aircraft fast enough - partly because imported GE engines keep arriving late - so despite huge headline growth potential, actual revenue has grown only modestly over the past five years. The stock is priced today as if the delivery ramp-up is a done deal, not a risk still playing out.
analysis.quarters: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 14.45% YoY to ₹5,515 crore and PAT rose 14.8% YoY to ₹1,589.66 crore, with margin expansion doing real work (EBITDA margin ~21.6% to ~27.7-28%), so this was not purely a volume story. Revenue and profit typically dip quarter-on-quarter in Q1 because Q4 is seasonally the strongest quarter for this company, which is normal and not a red flag. Specific guidance comments from the Q1 FY27 earnings call itself could not be independently verified from available sources - treat any FY27 margin/growth targets attributed to management as unconfirmed.
analysis.performance_read: The stock has returned 684% over 5 years and 172% over 3 years, well ahead of the Nifty (24% and 17% respectively) and modestly ahead of peer BEL over 5 years. Over the last 12 months the stock is roughly flat (+0.25%) while the Nifty fell 13.3%, so it has held up rather than cracked. It sits 13.1% below its July 2024 peak of ₹5,490.67 - a normal correction, not a crash, and there is no demerger or spin-off in the corporate-action history to distort this; the 2:1 split in September 2023 is a cosmetic share-count change that doesn't affect total-return comparisons.
analysis.valuation_read: At roughly 35x trailing earnings and about 8x book value, HAL is priced well above the market average. Why: a monopoly position in Indian military aviation, a debt-free balance sheet, a 24% ROE/32% ROCE, and a ₹2.54 lakh crore order book worth 7-8 years of current revenue. Whether that makes it cheap is a separate question - the price already assumes HAL executes on that backlog faster than its own 5-year track record (7.78% sales CAGR per Screener) suggests it has managed so far, so there is little margin of safety if delivery delays persist.
analysis.growth_read: Growth this quarter was both margin-led and volume-led - revenue grew 14.45% YoY and EBITDA margin expanded by roughly 6 percentage points at the same time, which is the more durable combination. The open question is whether this quarter's acceleration is a genuine step-up from order execution finally catching up, or a one-quarter blip, given the slower multi-year trend.
analysis.health_read: Profits are being generated at a high rate (24% ROE, debt-free balance sheet, no financial leverage risk), but working-capital days reportedly worsened from about 153 to 301 (per Screener.in, not independently cross-checked), which signals cash is taking longer to come in even as reported profit grows. The risk here is a business/execution risk - supply-chain bottlenecks like the GE engine delays - not a financial or solvency risk.
analysis.ownership_read: The Government of India holds 71.64% as promoter, a stable figure with no pledging, which is standard for a PSU and not a governance concern. Domestic institutions hold about 12.56% (rising) and foreign institutions about 9.42%. No marquee individual investor appears on the shareholding register based on available data - if a well-known name were expected here, it is not present.
strengths: Order book of ₹2.54 lakh crore as of March 2026, about 7-8x FY26 revenue, giving multi-year visibility
EBITDA margin expanded from ~21.6% to ~27.7-28% YoY in Q1 FY27 alongside 14.45% revenue growth
Debt-free balance sheet with ROE of 24% and ROCE of 32%
Monopoly-like position reinforced by milestones like the 2,000th aero-engine delivered in October 2026 and new engine-capacity investments (second Shakti line, AL-31FP expansion)
watchpoints: GE Aerospace's repeated F404-IN20 engine delivery shortfalls (3 delivered in August 2026 vs a 5-engine commitment) are the direct bottleneck delaying Tejas Mk1A handovers
Working-capital days reportedly nearly doubled (153 to 301 per Screener), a sign profit is not converting into cash as efficiently

Large pipeline items - the ~₹60,000-65,000 crore Su-30MKI 'Super Sukhoi' upgrade and the ~₹13,500 crore IMRH helicopter programme - are still awaiting formal CCS clearance and are not yet in the confirmed order book
Five-year revenue growth of only 7.78% (per Screener) despite a large order book shows execution, not demand, has been the historical constraint
analysis.one_thing: Whether HAL can convert its order book into actual deliveries on schedule - watch the pace of GE F404 engine deliveries and the Tejas Mk1A handover count through the Q2 FY27 results on November 3, 2026, since that is what will confirm or break the execution-acceleration story the current valuation is pricing in.
analysis.data_notes: Q1 FY27 revenue, PAT and margin figures were cross-checked across FreePressJournal, PSUConnect and Screener.in and were consistent. Valuation multiples (P/E, P/B, ROE, ROCE) are broadly consistent across Screener.in and ValueResearch. Could not independently verify: specific management guidance quotes from the Q1 FY27 earnings call transcript, the final CCS clearance status of the Su-30MKI 'Super Sukhoi' upgrade, the FY26 AGM date, and explicit confirmation of nil promoter pledging (assumed standard for a PSU but not separately disclosed in sources reviewed).
